To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bug tracking systems should provide: (i) assistance to users in reporting information to developers, and (ii) assistance to developers in understanding the context of a bug report.

the most important information needed by developers are (a) steps to reproduce, (b) a description of the problem and (c) the environment in which the problem occurs, while the most common problems faced by users are (a) not knowing what to report, (b) not knowing how to report and (c) not knowing what information to provide.
developers and users need to know what to report and how to report it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how we can make bug tracking easier for developers and users.
the question how bug tracking systems can be improved to help users and developers communicate more effectively.
the design of a bug tracking system, which is based on a better understanding of the information needs of bug reporters and bug resolvers, as well as the problems faced by them.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bug reporting systems should be designed to help developers and users to work together more effectively, and not as a tool to simply track bugs.
bug tracking systems are not only used to report bugs, but also to provide a forum for communication between developers and users.
bug tracking systems should be designed to help developers and users in the reporting process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

bug reports are not just bug reports, but rather a collection of information that is used for a variety of purposes by a variety of stakeholders, and that the design of bug tracking systems should take this into account.
developers and end-users have very different information needs and that the current generation of bug reporting tools does not support the information needs of either party.
the bug reporting process is currently very difficult for both end-users and developers and that the next generation of tools should provide support for the process.

bug reporting is a challenging process, and that developers need to be assisted by the bug tracking system to report bugs more efficiently.
